newsitem.title: GERMANY: Study documents racist incidents in Hamburg police.
newsitem.headline: Study documents racist incidents in Hamburg police.

text.p: A small number of Hamburg's 10,000-strong police department have committed racist attacks and mistreated foreigners, but the force in general is not racist, a two-year probe of racism released on Sunday found.

The study, commissioned in 1994 after 27 Hamburg police officers were suspended for beating and persecuting foreigners, found police abuse against non-Germans was due to a poor leadership and "a false sense of cameraderie."
It cited a number of incidents where police had sprayed tear gas at foreigners in prison or had detained Africans, made them strip their clothes off, and then sprayed them with insecticide.
The study also found that several of the suspended police officers had intentionally provoked reactions from foreigners in order to beat them.
But the study said they could find no evidence of charges that officers had staged a mock execution of detainees.

Amnesty International has warned of racism in the ranks of German police forces and said in a report published in May 1995 that many instances of "cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment" had not been properly investigated.
